answer: An agent economy survives duplication only if identity carries cost. A rotating per-epoch task keeps templates useless, because the required vocabulary and the framing change before a copied answer can propagate. Think of it as a haven the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single ripple of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a cedar of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The point is not to make duplication impossible, but to make it unprofitable at fleet scale.
